one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall inside the window. The first is the Q1 FY27 print. It is unconfirmed, but on the Oct-2025 and Oct-2024 pattern it very likely lands Wed Oct 28 or Thu Oct 29 after the close, before the Oct 30 scoring close. The Sep 2 8-K guide is revenue $89.85-90.95B, Azure +44-45% cc on the new definition and capex over $50B. The second is the Oct 27-28 FOMC. After the soft Sep 30 PCE print, swaps priced about a 36% hike chance per the supervisor's Bloomberg check, and the Sep 30 close (+1.8%) already reflects that print. For the print, the skeptic watch items are capex above $50B, the RPO mix (OpenAI is now about 40% of RPO, more than I had) and any sign OpenAI spend is moving to other clouds. These are weighed against a guide Microsoft usually beats, and the stock has run from $349 to near its high. I have no directional edge, so the ladder is centred on spot (P(>=518.28) about 0.50) at about 9.5% monthly sigma (32%/3.5, widened for the earnings gap), with slightly fat tails. This is essentially unchanged from round 1; the supervisor's findings concern the 12-month value, not the next four weeks.

fair_value.method: 70% P/E plus 30% FCF yield, both with a separate OpenAI stake. P/E: NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of $23.28 (FY28 $22.60, 4.5% below the $23.68 consensus) x 22x ex-stake = $512, plus about $28/share for the stake, less about $4.5/share of net debt including finance leases, gives $535. FCF yield: FY28 FCF of about $95B at 2.75%, less $33B net debt, over 7.43B shares = $461, plus $28 for the stake, gives $489. The blend is about $521, rounded to $520.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $23.68 less 4.5%, at the top of the 2-5% range the supervisor called defensible, down from my 9% cut in round 1. Reasons: about two-thirds of capex goes to short-lived servers and GPUs, whose depreciation ramps in FY28. Datacenter leases reclassified to operating now run through operating costs as lease expense. FY27 capex keeps growing even after the CY26 figure was cut by ~$15B through reclassification. I dropped the sec-api FY29 depreciation path as a driver because it is one third-party projection.
FY28 $22.60 grown about 12%, below consensus's ~20% FY28 growth, because FY29 carries the full depreciation of the FY27-28 builds.

Today: $518 less about $35 for the stake is about $483, over NTM EPS of about $20.7, which is about 23.3x. I take about 1.3 turns off. July PT cuts (Citi, Mizuho) cited software-wide multiple compression, capex runs at ~35% of revenue, and OpenAI is ~40% of RPO. That is still below the 26-30x the stock carried in 2023-25.

The 10-K gives an approximate 25% as-converted interest, not the 27% I used in round 1. At about $1.1T (midway between the $852B March round and the reported $1.4T talks) it is worth about $275B, or $37/share gross. I deduct 25% for tax and illiquidity, which gives about $28. The $1.4T round was only reported on 2026-09-29, is at an early stage and could change, and the IPO is delayed, so I do not mark to $1.4T.
Cash and short-term investments $76.8B, less debt at $40.3B book to $46.1B face, less finance leases $66.6B, gives $30-36B. I use the midpoint. The supervisor confirmed my round-1 treatment.

inputs_detail.derivation: OCF grows about 14-15% a year, from $183B to about $240B in FY28. This is net of operating-lease payments, which now absorb the reclassified datacenter spend. Cash PP&E capex rises to about $145B in FY28 (FY26 $116B; Q1 FY27 above $50B including finance leases). Because the reclassified leases reduce both capex and OCF, I count them once, in OCF. In round 1 I adjusted for them separately, which pushed my FCF off; that adjustment is now removed. Finance-lease principal is covered by the net-debt deduction.

bear.story: OpenAI is about 40% of the $678B RPO (roughly $270-281B), more than the one-third I assumed in round 1. Using its April-2026 any-cloud right, it moves incremental spend to AWS or others, or slows or reprices commitments if the $1.4T round stalls. Azure falls toward 30% while committed capex and $329B of uncommenced leases keep fixed costs rising. FY28 EPS comes in around $19.5-20 at 17-18x, plus a marked-down stake, which takes the stock back toward the $349 low.

base.story: Azure grows 35-40% while capacity constrained, and FY27 margin comes in down less than 1 point as guided. Server depreciation trims FY28 to about $22.6, a few percent under consensus. The ex-stake multiple eases to about 22x, and the OpenAI stake is marked near a $1.1T value. The stock ends modestly above spot.

bull.story: Copilot bundling lifts Office ARPU and the backlog converts on time. OpenAI's round closes at about $1.4T or better, which marks the 25% stake to about $47/share gross and eases the funding fears. EPS reaches about $24.5 at 27-28x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $400 (-23%) the stock would be at about 18x my haircut FY28 EPS of $22.60, or about 20x FY27 consensus, and under about 17x after subtracting the stake. At that level the market would be pricing a real break rather than volatility: OpenAI cutting, delaying or repricing its roughly $270-280B of RPO under its any-cloud rights; Azure below about 30%; or FY27-28 capex still rising while revenue guidance falls. The stock did reach $349 in 2026 with earnings intact, so I would confirm a break with estimate cuts, not price alone.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor showed that my round-1 fair value ($485, the only one below spot) came mainly from an unsourced 9% FY28 EPS cut. I accept that. Management guides FY27 operating margin down less than 1 point and says the useful-life change gives only a minimal FY27 benefit, so my 'accounting cushion' argument was overstated. I now use $22.60, 4.5% under the $23.68 consensus: a skeptic's haircut, but a sourced one. I also accept the other corrections. The stake is about 25%, not 27%. The ~$175B capex figure is calendar-2026 (I verified this on TIKR/Yahoo), and FY27 capex still grows. I now value the OpenAI stake explicitly, at about $28/share net, using a $1.1T midpoint between the March $852B round and the reported early-stage $1.4T talks. I also rebuilt the FCF leg so the operating-lease shift is counted once. That gives a fair value of about $520, roughly at spot, up from $485. Two findings cut the other way, and I keep the bear component because of them. First, OpenAI's RPO share is about 38-41%, not the one-third I had; I agree with the supervisor's bound. Second, FY27 spending is higher than I assumed. The skeptic facts also stand: $329B of uncommenced leases, a zero-Sell consensus, and FCF that fell two years running. Where I still differ from the supervisor ($550): I keep a haircut toward 5% rather than 3%, and I do not mark the stake above $1.1T before a round closes. Distribution: a mixture of 80% lognormal (median $545, sigma 0.27) and a 20% bear component (median $390, sigma 0.26). That gives P(>=518) of about 0.49 (0.44 in round 1), a median of about $513, and a fatter left tail than a symmetric 32%-vol lognormal. Scenario mean is about $545. Round 2 used 1 search and 3 fetches (the call transcript, TIKR/Yahoo, and search results on the OpenAI round). The MS blog, CNBC Q2 and 10-K stake figures are taken from the supervisor's fact-check and not re-fetched.
